title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is part of Grothendieck's 'Récapitulation' on the group \hat{\mathfrak{S}}_{0,3}, the extension 1 -> \pi_{0,3} -> \mathfrak{S}_{0,3} -> T_{0,3} -> 1. Here T_{0,3} ≅ S_3 × Z/2 is the full group of conformal and anticonformal automorphisms of (P^1_C, {0,1,∞}).

This page finishes describing T_{0,3}.
- The centre Z/2 is generated by complex conjugation τ(z) = z̄.
- The five other non-holomorphic elements are τσ_0, τσ_1, τσ_∞, τρ and τρ^{-1}.
- Three of them are anticonformal involutions: τ'_0(z) = z̄/(z̄−1), τ'_1(z) = 1/z̄, τ'_∞(z) = 1−z̄.

He lists the fixed-point sets.
- Fixed points of the holomorphic elements: σ_0 → {0, 2}; σ_1 → {1, −1}; σ_∞ → {∞, 1/2}; ρ and ρ^{-1} → {−j̄, −j}, the primitive 6th roots of unity e^{±iπ/3}.
- The order-6 anti-automorphisms ρτ and ρ^{-1}τ are fixed-point free.
- Fixed loci of the anti-involutions:
  - τ → P^1(R);
  - τ'_0 → circle (x−1)^2 + y^2 = 1;
  - τ'_1 → unit circle;
  - τ'_∞ → line Re z = 1/2.

Geometric picture on the Riemann sphere. τ is reflection in the 'equator' P^1(R). The three τ'_i are reflections in three 'meridian' great circles through the 'poles' −j̄ and −j. These meridians cut the equator into six arcs at 0, 1/2, 1, 2, ∞, −1.

Formulas (10): ρ permutes the τ'_i cyclically by conjugation, and τ'_0τ'_1 = τ'_1τ'_∞ = τ'_∞τ'_0 = ρ.

Purpose (visible on the next page): the four circles tile the sphere into 12 spherical triangles with angles π/2, π/3, π/2. These are fundamental domains, exhibiting T_{0,3} as the Coxeter group A_1×A_2. The stabiliser of the base point −j̄ is the 'twisted' S_3' = {1, τ'_0, τ'_1, τ'_∞, ρ, ρ^{-1}}, which mixes holomorphic and antiholomorphic elements. It acts on π_1(P^1 − {0,1,∞}; −j̄), and this action is used to describe 'lacet' automorphisms of \hat{π}_{0,3} together with complex conjugation.
errors: Notation wobbles between \dot\tau_i in (6) and \dot\tau'_i in (7) for the same anti-involutions τσ_i. This is cosmetic.
The inline description of P^1_R as {z | z + z̄ = 2z̄} is a clumsy way to write z = z̄, though still correct. The trailing marks after it are unreadable.
All formulas I checked are correct: the fixed points of σ_i, ρ, the τ'_i and ρτ; the circle loci; the conjugation relations; and τ'_iτ'_{i+1} = ρ.

ideas.what: Full (anti)conformal symmetry group of (P^1, {0,1,∞}) as S_3 × Z/2, with explicit anti-involutions and their fixed circles
ideas.modern_name: Anharmonic group extended by complex conjugation; real structures of P^1 − {0,1,∞}

ideas.what: Picture of T_{0,3} as a reflection group on the sphere generated by reflections in an equator and three meridians through the 6th roots of unity
ideas.modern_name: Spherical Coxeter group A_1×A_2 (triangle group (2,2,3)); barycentric subdivision of the two hemispheres

ideas.what: Choice of the ρ-fixed point −j̄ = e^{iπ/3} as a symmetric base point, whose stabiliser is a twisted S_3 mixing holomorphic and antiholomorphic maps acting on π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: Symmetric base point for S_3 action on the free (profinite) group of P^1−{0,1,∞}, incorporating complex conjugation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Related ideas appear in work on GT and complex conjugation (Ihara, Drinfeld, Lochak–Schneps)

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary, correct recapitulation of the classical symmetry group of the thrice-punctured sphere and its reflection-group picture. The only mildly distinctive feature is the systematic use of the anti-holomorphic twisted S_3 stabilising −j̄ as the acting group on π_{0,3}, which is a natural, known device.
transcription_corrections: In (8), the margin note reads 'NB P^{1 ρτ}_C = P^{1 ρ^{-1}τ}_C = ∅' (written vertically); the exponents are ρ^τ-type composites, as transcribed.
Equation (6) is labelled '(6)' with an earlier crossed-out label; its elements are τσ̇_0 = τ̇_0, etc.

The label next to the circle for τ'_0 ('= ½ − U' in the transcription) is unclear. Mathematically it is the circle centred at 1 of radius 1, i.e. 1 + U; the label after the unit-circle description reads '= U'.
